item_format: pick which of 4 options is a pure rotation (not a mirror image) of a target 3D cube (Shepard-Metzler) figure
cognitive_process: 3D mental rotation and mirror-vs-rotation discrimination
engagement_affordance: drag to spin the block figure in 3D before locking an answer; framed as match-the-crystal with a satisfying snap when the correct orientation is found
adaptivity_fit: high - rotation angle, rotation axis, and number of cubes are fully parameterizable for automatic item generation (AIG)
tail_discrimination: high - large angular disparity plus more cubes and added mirror foils cleanly separate top performers
coachability_bias_risk: low language load so strong for ELL; training effects exist (Uttal 2013 g=0.47) but transfer and are durable; watch documented sex differences as a fairness check
advantage_vs_cogat: CogAT barely measures true 3D rotation (its nonverbal battery is figural reasoning, Lohman 2005); adding it captures STEM talent CogAT misses (Wai/Lubinski/Benbow 2009 SMPY) and is naturally interactive
source_name: Vandenberg & Kuse Mental Rotations Test (redraws of Shepard-Metzler figures)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - redrawn Shepard-Metzler figures are widely reused in research

item_format: a worked example shows an object rotated a given way; pick the option that applies the same rotation to a new 3D object (isometric drawings)
cognitive_process: analogical 3D rotation (infer and reapply a rotation rule)
engagement_affordance: tablet drag-to-rotate preview of the sample rotation; learner replays the spin like a short animation before choosing
adaptivity_fit: high - rotation magnitude, axis count (single vs combined), and symmetric-vs-asymmetric solids are IRT-tunable (PSVT:R difficulty maps to complexity)
tail_discrimination: high - asymmetric figures and multi-axis rotations resist guessing and stretch the top tail
coachability_bias_risk: med - analytic strategies can be coached, so use AIG novel figures; low reading load aids ELL fairness
advantage_vs_cogat: targets rotation-of-rotation reasoning central to engineering and chemistry that CogAT does not isolate; PSVT:R is a documented STEM predictor
source_name: Revised Purdue Spatial Visualization Test: Rotations (Guay 1977; Yoon 2011)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - author original figures in the PSVT:R style rather than copying plates

item_format: two 3D block figures shown at varying angular disparity; decide same vs different (mirror) as fast as possible
cognitive_process: chronometric 3D rotation (response time scales with angular disparity)
engagement_affordance: beat-the-clock same/different tapping game; a live speed meter rewards fast-accurate judgments and visualizes the linear RT-by-angle effect
adaptivity_fit: high - angular disparity is a continuous difficulty dial and RT gives a graded latent-trait signal ideal for adaptive testing
tail_discrimination: high - combining accuracy and reaction time at large angles finely ranks high performers beyond ceiling
coachability_bias_risk: med - speeded format is practice-sensitive; mitigate with fresh AIG figures; minimal language demand supports ELL fairness
advantage_vs_cogat: CogAT is untimed figural reasoning and cannot capture rotation speed or efficiency, the hallmark of spatial talent linked to STEM
source_name: Shepard & Metzler, Mental rotation of three-dimensional objects (Science, 1971)
reuse_note: adapt_ok - foundational paradigm; generate original block figures

item_format: a familiar animal shape appears rotated in the picture plane; child decides if it is the same animal or a flipped (mirror) version
cognitive_process: 2D mental rotation with concrete, nameable stimuli
engagement_affordance: tap the right-way-up vs backwards animal; an optional drag-to-rotate training mode lets young children spin the animal upright themselves
adaptivity_fit: high - rotation angle and shape familiarity scale difficulty down for early grades
tail_discrimination: med - young-child ceilings limit tail spread; larger angles and less-familiar shapes extend range
coachability_bias_risk: low - concrete animals reduce vocabulary load, good for ELL and pre-readers; brief practice improves scores but generalizes
advantage_vs_cogat: gives K-2 a genuine rotation measure at an age when CogAT relies on picture reasoning; early spatial skill forecasts later math
